pathway.title: Bellring Brands, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate: scale and brand strength support cash flow, but concentration limits its durability. Net sales were USD 2,354.6 million over the last twelve months, up 1.64% on fiscal 2025, with Premier Protein 85.9% of sales and ready-to-drink shakes 81.7%; three retailers took 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales with no material long-term supply agreements. Growth has slowed from 16.05% in fiscal 2025 to 2.28% in the nine months, so the business now depends on holding shelf space more than adding it. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 31; calculation C2

Margin resilience is weak at present. Gross margin fell to 28.59% over the last twelve months from 33.26% in fiscal 2025 and EBITDA margin to 14.10% from 16.23%, as cost of goods sold rose to 71.53% of net sales in the nine months with a USD 11.3 million ingredient charge and a USD 10.0 million inventory reserve. Premier Protein's average net selling price fell because of promotion and mix, so cost inflation is not being recovered through price on the main brand: EBITDA fell 11.73% while net sales rose 1.64%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 22; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4

Free cash flow conversion is solid, carried by low capital needs more than by earnings. Free cash flow was USD 225.0 million over the last twelve months, 67.79% of EBITDA against 68.06% in fiscal 2025, because additions to property were only 0.20% of fiscal 2025 net sales. Two items weigh on the next period: inventory absorbed USD 150.7 million of operating cash in the nine months, and the USD 86.0 million legal payment equals 38.22% of last-twelve-month free cash flow. Fiscal 2025 free cash flow does not yet carry the cash cost of the USD 69.0 million legal provision, which was accrued and not paid. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 90, 98; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 16; calculation C3; calculation C6

Leverage is moderate but rising, and covenant headroom cannot be established. Total debt was 3.42x last-twelve-month EBITDA at 30 June 2026 against 2.88x at the 2025 year end, and net leverage was 3.27x, or 3.53x pro forma for the USD 86.0 million payment due on 10 August 2026, with net debt of USD 1,084.9 million rising to USD 1,170.9 million pro forma. EBITDA covered interest expense 4.20x over the last twelve months against 5.50x in fiscal 2025. The financial covenant stated is a maximum total net leverage ratio of 6.00 times under a definition that is not supplied, so the ratios here are not the covenant measure and headroom is not calculable. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 95, 101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 19; calculation C5; calculation C10

Liquidity and refinancing risk are contained for about three years. Liquidity of USD 248.0 million at 30 June 2026 is down 22.69% from USD 320.8 million at the 2024 year end, and the effect of the legal payment on liquidity is not established in Financial foundation. Both debt instruments fall due within fiscal 2030: the 7.00% senior notes of USD 840.0 million on 15 March 2030, and the revolver, USD 300.0 million drawn, on 22 August 2030 or 14 December 2029 if the notes are not refinanced, which is 3.07 years after the as-of date. The interest run-rate on principal debt is USD 75.7 million a year, so a refinancing at a higher rate or on lower EBITDA would add to the burden. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 93–95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13, 32; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C11

Financial policy and governance are the swing factor, and the risk level is Medium. Business & governance finds repurchases of USD 474.9 million in fiscal 2025, or 185.58% of free cash flow, with USD 300.0 million of net revolver borrowing over fiscal 2025 and the nine months and USD 506.9 million of authorisation remaining at 30 June 2026, while the chairman holds a role at Post, the chief executive gave notice of retirement and securities suits are pending. There is no sponsor extracting value and no dividend, and repurchases paused in May and June 2026. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 53, 76–77; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 33

The primary downside path runs from retailer concentration through volume to fixed costs. A retailer reducing distribution or moving volume to a competing brand would cut net sales while take-or-pay commitments of USD 1,362.9 million, of which USD 602.7 million fall due in fiscal 2026 and equal 38.98% of fiscal 2025 cost of goods sold, and contract manufacturer minimums stay in place; with margin already compressed, EBITDA and free cash flow would fall faster than sales, leverage above 3.42x would follow and the revolver would fund the gap. No stress figure is given because the filings do not disclose customer-level terms. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14, 31, 66–67; calculation C7

runs.text: Strengths, in rank order. First, asset-light cash generation: additions to property were 0.20% of fiscal 2025 net sales and free cash flow was 67.79% of EBITDA over the last twelve months, so cash is available for debt service even as earnings fall, which supports debt service capacity. Second, liquidity and maturity runway: liquidity of USD 248.0 million and a first maturity 3.07 years away limit refinancing and liquidity risk in the near term. Third, brand scale: Premier Protein is 85.9% of sales and net sales grew 16.05% in fiscal 2025 and 2.28% in the nine months, which supports revenue durability while distribution holds. Fourth, no sponsor extraction and no dividend, so cash is not leaving through fees or distributions other than repurchases. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 53, 76; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C9

Weaknesses, in rank order. First, customer concentration: three retailers took 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales with no material long-term agreements, so one decision can remove a large share of revenue. Second, margin compression: EBITDA margin fell to 14.10% from 16.23% and cost of goods sold rose to 71.53% of net sales in the nine months, which cuts cash flow available for debt service. Third, rising leverage with shareholder returns above free cash flow: total debt to EBITDA rose to 3.42x from 2.88x while repurchases were 185.58% of free cash flow in fiscal 2025. Fourth, supply concentration and related-party reliance: one manufacturer made 46.3% of shake supply and shakes bought from a Post subsidiary reached 6.60% of nine-month cost of goods sold. Fifth, event risk from litigation, a USD 86.0 million legal payment and a leadership transition. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 16–19; calculation C1

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only transaction in the supplied filings is the March 2022 spin-off from Post, and it set the capital structure that still stands. BellRing issued USD 840.0 million of 7.00% senior notes due 2030 at par on 10 March 2022 with USD 10.2 million of issuance costs and entered a USD 250.0 million revolving credit facility the same day, while Post contributed its units and USD 550.4 million of cash in exchange for the right to receive the notes and equity interests in BellRing. Post distributed 80.1% of its stake to its own shareholders and the dual-class structure of the former listed company was eliminated. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 93

The one later change to the debt documents is the first amendment of 22 August 2025. It raised the revolving commitments to USD 500.0 million, extended maturity to 22 August 2030 (14 December 2029 if the notes are not redeemed or refinanced by then), lowered the margin and broadened exceptions to the covenants that restrict activities such as stock repurchases. Revolver borrowing was USD 700.0 million and repayment USD 450.0 million in fiscal 2025, and USD 325.0 million and USD 275.0 million in the nine months to 30 June 2026, so principal debt rose from USD 840.0 million at 30 September 2024 to USD 1,140.0 million at 30 June 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 65, 93–95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10; calculation C11; calculation C21

No acquisition, sale of a business or new debt issue is described after the spin-off, apart from the discontinuance of PowerBar in North America, and no offering document, sources and uses or sponsor transaction is supplied, so entry valuation and sponsor economics are not established. Management says further long-term financing needs depend on growth opportunities that include acquisition activity, which is management language and not a plan. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt to EBITDA rose from 1.96x at the 2024 year end to 2.88x at the 2025 year end and 3.42x on a last-twelve-month basis at 30 June 2026. The fiscal 2025 step came from carrying debt rising from USD 833.1 million to USD 1,084.3 million while EBITDA fell from USD 424.2 million to USD 376.0 million after a USD 69.0 million legal provision. The later step came from debt reaching USD 1,185.0 million in March 2026 and last-twelve-month EBITDA falling to USD 310.7 million before recovering to USD 331.9 million, as the weak third quarter of fiscal 2025, which carried the provision, left the window. Set aside that provision and fiscal 2025 leverage would have been 2.44x, so underlying leverage has risen by nearly one turn against a reported rise of about half a turn. The mechanism is a lower gross margin combined with share repurchases that exceeded free cash flow and were part funded by the revolver, which leaves less cushion for the legal payment now due.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid rose from USD 59.6 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 68.3 million in fiscal 2025, and EBITDA cover fell from 7.12x to 5.51x. Interest expense, net was USD 60.0 million in the nine months to 30 June 2026 against USD 49.3 million a year earlier because revolver borrowing rose, and the weighted-average rate on total debt was 6.7% in the third quarter. The 7.00% senior notes carry a fixed cost, so the floating revolver, at 5.62% on the drawn amount at 30 June 2026, is the variable element. Cash interest paid is printed only for fiscal years, so cover for the last twelve months is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 65.0 million in the nine months to 30 June 2026 against USD 91.5 million a year earlier, because inventory absorbed USD 150.7 million of cash and earnings fell. Free cash flow of USD 56.9 million covered less than half of the USD 137.2 million spent on share repurchases; the rest came from USD 50.0 million of net revolver borrowing and a USD 38.1 million fall in cash including restricted cash. Capital expenditure is small, at USD 8.1 million in the nine months, so the lever available to creditors is repurchase policy rather than capital spending.

fields.value: Liquidity at 30 June 2026 was USD 248.0 million, made up of USD 50.4 million of unrestricted cash and USD 197.6 million undrawn on the USD 500.0 million revolver after USD 2.4 million of letters of credit, against USD 320.8 million at the 2024 year end. The USD 86.0 million of legal settlement payments due by 10 August 2026 equal 34.68% of that liquidity, and net debt would rise to USD 1,170.9 million, or 3.53x last-twelve-month EBITDA, once they are paid. No facility matures within twelve months of the as-of date, because the notes fall due on 15 March 2030 and the revolver on 22 August 2030, or 14 December 2029 if the notes are not refinanced, so the near-term pressure is on liquidity rather than refinancing.

fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that net sales still grew in the nine months to 30 June 2026, last-twelve-month EBITDA recovered in the third quarter as the prior-year provision left the window, no debt matures before December 2029, and the revolver still has USD 197.6 million undrawn. That evidence would win if gross margin recovers toward its fiscal 2025 level and repurchases slow, which would reverse the rise in leverage; it loses if inventory keeps absorbing cash and the legal payment is funded by further borrowing.

fields.value: The largest gap is the fiscal 2026 annual report: until it is supplied, leverage and liquidity stop at 30 June 2026 and the effect of the August payment and any later revolver draw cannot be seen. The absence of an issuer-stated EBITDA and of the Credit Agreement definitions means covenant headroom is not calculable, and the net debt ratio here must not be read as the covenant measure, because the covenant is a total net leverage ratio of at most 6.00:1.00 whose reported value is not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fiscal 2026 annual report and fourth-quarter results are not supplied, so every balance-sheet figure stops at 30 June 2026 and the fiscal 2026 year-end position is not established; this restricts net debt, leverage and liquidity to the quarter-end balance sheet. Severity: High. Action: supply the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA in any supplied filing, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived for every period as operating profit plus depreciation and amortization; this restricts every leverage and cover ratio and the revenue and EBITDA chart to a derived definition, and leaves the EBITDA bridge unstated. Severity: High. Action: supply an earnings release or other document that states the issuer's EBITDA and any adjustments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The USD 86.0 million of legal settlement payments due on or before 10 August 2026 fall after the last balance sheet, and whether they were paid and how they were funded is not stated; this restricts quoted net debt, which is shown beside a pro forma row. Severity: High. Action: confirm the payments and their funding from the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Credit Agreement's total net leverage ratio is not defined in the supplied text and the reported ratio is not printed, only the maximum of 6.00:1.00 and a statement of compliance; covenant headroom is therefore not calculable, and the net debt to EBITDA ratio in this module is a different measure. Severity: High. Action: supply the executed Credit Agreement and the compliance certificate.

fields.value: - Cash interest paid is printed for fiscal years only, so EBITDA to cash interest is not calculable at 31 December 2025, 31 March 2026 or 30 June 2026 and the last-twelve-month cover is not established; interest expense is not substituted. Severity: Medium. Action: supply cash interest paid for the interim periods or the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Bellring Brands, Inc. (issuer brbr-1772016) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. It sets out what the company sells and to whom, who owns and governs it, how it is supplied and funded, and which dated events changed its credit risk, from the five supplied filings and the source readiness assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed as a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BellRing's creditors face a concentrated, asset-light brand business whose main governance risk is shareholder returns, not an owner: repurchases outran free cash flow while revolver debt rose, and the discretion to repeat that decides how fast leverage moves. Three customers bought 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales without material long-term supply agreements, one contract manufacturer made 46.3% of Premier Protein shake supply, and repurchases of USD 474.9 million in fiscal 2025 were 185.58% of free cash flow of USD 255.9 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 12, 14, 76–77; calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Post sold its last shares in 2022, so no sponsor is identified behind the credit, but the chairman still holds a Post role, the chief executive gave notice of retirement, a different person certifies the latest report and securities suits are pending. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: the evidence is mixed and the proxy statement that would show board independence and large holders is missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 45, 104–105; 10-Q_2025-12-31_brbr_brbr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-03-31_brbr_brbr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 34; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is the main business risk behind the credit. Three customers took 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales (34.3%, 27.5% and 12.2%), the issuer has no material long-term supply agreements with customers and customers frequently reevaluate the products they carry, so one retailer's decision on shelf space or on a competing brand can remove a large share of sales. Costs do not flex in step: take-or-pay purchase commitments were USD 1,362.9 million at 30 September 2025, with USD 602.7 million due in fiscal 2026. How much of that commitment could be resized is not stated, so the link from lost sales to cash flow is an analyst inference. The issuer attributes the 16.05% growth in fiscal 2025 net sales to distribution gains and promotion, so growth and concentration have come together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 31, 64, 66–67, 87; calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supply is concentrated and part of it now comes from the former parent. One contract manufacturer made 46.3% of Premier Protein shake supply in fiscal 2025 and a single facility of it made 28.0%, one supplier provides the majority of milk-based protein, and a sole supplier provides the aseptic packaging for the 11 ounce shake. Purchases of shakes from Comet, a subsidiary of Post, rose from USD 8.6 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 62.2 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 80.6 million in the nine months to 30 June 2026, which is 6.60% of nine-month cost of goods sold against 4.07% a year earlier, and the payable to Post and its subsidiaries reached USD 15.0 million. The filings say licences with Post are priced as arm's-length transactions but give no pricing basis for the Comet purchases, so related-party pricing is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 23–26, 87; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 7; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns, not an owner, are the governance risk that moves creditor outcomes. Cash repurchases were USD 474.9 million in fiscal 2025, or 185.58% of free cash flow of USD 255.9 million, and USD 137.2 million in the nine months to 30 June 2026, or 241.12% of free cash flow of USD 56.9 million. Across fiscal 2025 and the nine months repurchases exceeded free cash flow by USD 299.3 million while net revolver borrowing was USD 300.0 million, and in August 2025 the lenders agreed to a USD 500.0 million revolver with broadened exceptions for stock repurchases. The issuer does not link the borrowing to the repurchases, so that funding is an analyst inference from the cash flows. Board authorisations rose from USD 300.0 million to USD 400.0 million and then USD 600.0 million between March and November 2025, and USD 506.9 million of the latest remained at 30 June 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 65, 76–77, 93; 10-Q_2025-12-31_brbr_brbr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 33–34; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is identified in the filings, but overlap with Post persists. Post held about 14.2% after the March 2022 spin-off and sold its last shares on 25 November 2022; the chairman of the board still serves as an officer and director of Post, the charter lets Post and its affiliates compete and renounces corporate opportunities for overlapping directors while any Post-affiliated person serves, and a tax matters agreement obliges BellRing to indemnify Post for tax liabilities that follow from its own actions. With no sponsor there is no named source of equity support in the filings, and with the proxy statement missing the independence of the board and the presence of any large holder are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management and legal events add event risk without yet showing a failure of controls. The chief executive gave notice of retirement on 2 February 2026, effective at the earlier of a successor's appointment or the end of fiscal 2026 on 30 September 2026, and the chief executive certification of the report signed on 4 August 2026 is given by a different person whose title and appointment date are not stated, so a change of chief executive between May and August 2026 is likely but not documented; the end of fiscal 2026 itself fell 49 days before the as-of date. A securities class action and a consolidated derivative action allege misstatements between August 2024 and May 2026; the court granted in part and denied in part the motion to dismiss on 28 July 2026 and the company cannot estimate a loss. The older Joint Juice litigation is settled for USD 90.0 million, of which USD 86.0 million remained to be paid on or before 10 August 2026, and the provision sits in fiscal 2025 results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2025-12-31_brbr_brbr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-03-31_brbr_brbr-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18, 34; 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 98; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is asset-light, but growth and margin have turned. Net sales growth slowed from 19.76% in fiscal 2024 and 16.05% in fiscal 2025 to 2.28% in the nine months to 30 June 2026, because Premier Protein sales rose USD 6.4 million on 5% higher volume offset by lower prices from promotion, while Dymatize sales rose 14%. Cost of goods sold rose from 65.06% of net sales in the nine months to 30 June 2025 to 71.53%, a rise of 6.47 percentage points that includes a USD 11.3 million charge for an ingredient that failed quality requirements and a USD 10.0 million inventory reserve. Capital spending was only 0.20% of net sales in fiscal 2025, so cost pressure lands on cash flow, not on capital outlay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 76, 86; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 19, 22, 25; calculation C2; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Board structure gives creditors little protection beyond the debt documents, and those documents are not supplied. The board is split into three classes until the 2027 annual meeting, directors can be removed only for cause, preferred stock can be issued without a stockholder vote and an exclusive Delaware forum applies, which together make a board reset slow. The restated charter and bylaws were filed with the Form 8-K of 31 January 2025, while the Credit Agreement and indenture appear only as exhibit references, so how much more stock the company may buy back under its restricted-payment terms is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, sponsor and governance risk is Medium. The behaviour that matters is repurchases above free cash flow funded in part by the revolver, which matters because it raises debt while the company faces a USD 86.0 million legal payment and slowing sales, and it implies higher refinancing and liquidity risk if repeated. Countervailing evidence is that there is no sponsor extracting value, no cash dividend has ever been paid, the services agreement with Post ended with its functions transferred and repurchases paused in May and June 2026. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit documents and the reports for fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that no sponsor extracts value and no cash dividend has been paid: Post sold its stake in 2022, related-party service fees were only USD 3.0 million in fiscal 2025 and ended with the services agreement in March 2026, internal control over financial reporting was audited as effective at 30 September 2025, and no shares were repurchased in May or June 2026 after the April average price of USD 15.66 per share. The brand business also still grows, at 2.28% in the nine months, with Dymatize sales up 14%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 53, 87, 102; 10-Q_2026-03-31_brbr_brbr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 22, 33; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the proxy statement shows a majority of independent directors and no large holder, if the new chief executive adopts a leverage target that caps repurchases, or if repurchases stay paused while free cash flow recovers. It would worsen if repurchases resume under the USD 506.9 million of authorisation remaining while the revolver is drawn, if a major retailer cuts distribution, or if the partial denial of the motion to dismiss leads to a settlement that is large against free cash flow of USD 56.9 million in the nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee roles, any large holder and executive pay are not established, and the Medium governance rating could move either way once they are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed Credit Agreement and indenture are not supplied, so restricted-payment capacity is not established; the conclusion that repurchases are the main shareholder-return risk rests on observed behaviour and would weaken if the baskets prove narrow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Evidence ends with the quarterly report signed on 4 August 2026, so the terms of the chief executive succession, the legal payment due by 10 August 2026, any repurchase or borrowing after June 2026 and fiscal 2026 results are not seen, and the management and repurchase conclusions describe the position at that signature date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pricing and terms of the Comet purchases are not stated, so the conclusion that related-party supply is a dependence and not a transfer of value cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer names are not tied to their shares of net sales and no retailer contract terms are supplied, so the concentration conclusion cannot be sized for any single retailer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The nature of the reorganisation charges in the nine months to 30 June 2026 is not described, so the margin conclusion cannot say whether they recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only transaction in the supplied filings is the March 2022 spin-off from Post, and it set the capital structure that still stands. BellRing issued USD 840.0 million of 7.00% senior notes due 2030 at par on 10 March 2022 with USD 10.2 million of issuance costs and entered a USD 250.0 million revolving credit facility the same day, while Post contributed its units and USD 550.4 million of cash in exchange for the right to receive the notes and equity interests in BellRing. Post distributed 80.1% of its stake to its own shareholders and the dual-class structure of the former listed company was eliminated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one later change to the debt documents is the first amendment of 22 August 2025. It raised the revolving commitments to USD 500.0 million, extended maturity to 22 August 2030 (14 December 2029 if the notes are not redeemed or refinanced by then), lowered the margin and broadened exceptions to the covenants that restrict activities such as stock repurchases. Revolver borrowing was USD 700.0 million and repayment USD 450.0 million in fiscal 2025, and USD 325.0 million and USD 275.0 million in the nine months to 30 June 2026, so principal debt rose from USD 840.0 million at 30 September 2024 to USD 1,140.0 million at 30 June 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 65, 93–95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10; calculation C11; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition, sale of a business or new debt issue is described after the spin-off, apart from the discontinuance of PowerBar in North America, and no offering document, sources and uses or sponsor transaction is supplied, so entry valuation and sponsor economics are not established. Management says further long-term financing needs depend on growth opportunities that include acquisition activity, which is management language and not a plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No conflict between the supplied filings was found that changes a conclusion; the conflict log shows the differences found and how each was kept. This answer corrects one point in the source readiness assessment: the signature pages of the annual reports do name the directors, seven at both year ends, so what is missing is their independence, holdings and pay. The gaps below are missing documents, missing events and fidelity limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Bellring Brands, Inc. (issuer brbr-1772016) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the business profile, margin, cash flow, leverage, liquidity, refinancing and governance into one credit view, with a ranked set of drivers and monitoring triggers, from the five supplied filings and the three earlier assessments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed as a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BellRing's credit profile is adequate but weakening: a cash-generative, asset-light brand franchise still supports the debt, yet margin compression, repurchases above free cash flow and dependence on three retailers have lifted leverage and left little room for error.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 31; calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt was 3.42x last-twelve-month EBITDA at 30 June 2026 against 2.88x at the 2025 year end, and net leverage was 3.27x, or 3.53x pro forma for the USD 86.0 million legal payment due on 10 August 2026. Liquidity of USD 248.0 million and no debt maturity before December 2029 contain the near-term risk. The primary downside path is a retailer cutting distribution while margins stay compressed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13, 16; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: scale and brand strength support cash flow, but concentration limits its durability. Net sales were USD 2,354.6 million over the last twelve months, up 1.64% on fiscal 2025, with Premier Protein 85.9% of sales and ready-to-drink shakes 81.7%; three retailers took 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales with no material long-term supply agreements. Growth has slowed from 16.05% in fiscal 2025 to 2.28% in the nine months, so the business now depends on holding shelf space more than adding it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 31; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is weak at present. Gross margin fell to 28.59% over the last twelve months from 33.26% in fiscal 2025 and EBITDA margin to 14.10% from 16.23%, as cost of goods sold rose to 71.53% of net sales in the nine months with a USD 11.3 million ingredient charge and a USD 10.0 million inventory reserve. Premier Protein's average net selling price fell because of promotion and mix, so cost inflation is not being recovered through price on the main brand: EBITDA fell 11.73% while net sales rose 1.64%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 22; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow conversion is solid, carried by low capital needs more than by earnings. Free cash flow was USD 225.0 million over the last twelve months, 67.79% of EBITDA against 68.06% in fiscal 2025, because additions to property were only 0.20% of fiscal 2025 net sales. Two items weigh on the next period: inventory absorbed USD 150.7 million of operating cash in the nine months, and the USD 86.0 million legal payment equals 38.22% of last-twelve-month free cash flow. Fiscal 2025 free cash flow does not yet carry the cash cost of the USD 69.0 million legal provision, which was accrued and not paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 90, 98; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 16; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate but rising, and covenant headroom cannot be established. Total debt was 3.42x last-twelve-month EBITDA at 30 June 2026 against 2.88x at the 2025 year end, and net leverage was 3.27x, or 3.53x pro forma for the USD 86.0 million payment due on 10 August 2026, with net debt of USD 1,084.9 million rising to USD 1,170.9 million pro forma. EBITDA covered interest expense 4.20x over the last twelve months against 5.50x in fiscal 2025. The financial covenant stated is a maximum total net leverage ratio of 6.00 times under a definition that is not supplied, so the ratios here are not the covenant measure and headroom is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 95, 101; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 19; calculation C5; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and refinancing risk are contained for about three years. Liquidity of USD 248.0 million at 30 June 2026 is down 22.69% from USD 320.8 million at the 2024 year end, and the effect of the legal payment on liquidity is not established in Financial foundation. Both debt instruments fall due within fiscal 2030: the 7.00% senior notes of USD 840.0 million on 15 March 2030, and the revolver, USD 300.0 million drawn, on 22 August 2030 or 14 December 2029 if the notes are not refinanced, which is 3.07 years after the as-of date. The interest run-rate on principal debt is USD 75.7 million a year, so a refinancing at a higher rate or on lower EBITDA would add to the burden.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 93–95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13, 32; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are the swing factor, and the risk level is Medium. Business & governance finds repurchases of USD 474.9 million in fiscal 2025, or 185.58% of free cash flow, with USD 300.0 million of net revolver borrowing over fiscal 2025 and the nine months and USD 506.9 million of authorisation remaining at 30 June 2026, while the chairman holds a role at Post, the chief executive gave notice of retirement and securities suits are pending. There is no sponsor extracting value and no dividend, and repurchases paused in May and June 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path runs from retailer concentration through volume to fixed costs. A retailer reducing distribution or moving volume to a competing brand would cut net sales while take-or-pay commitments of USD 1,362.9 million, of which USD 602.7 million fall due in fiscal 2026 and equal 38.98% of fiscal 2025 cost of goods sold, and contract manufacturer minimums stay in place; with margin already compressed, EBITDA and free cash flow would fall faster than sales, leverage above 3.42x would follow and the revolver would fund the gap. No stress figure is given because the filings do not disclose customer-level terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14, 31, 66–67; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that cash generation has held while earnings fell: free cash flow was 67.79% of EBITDA over the last twelve months, above 46.63% in fiscal 2024, net sales still grew 2.28% in the nine months with Dymatize sales up 14%, and the company paused repurchases in May and June 2026. Liquidity of USD 248.0 million and a first maturity more than three years away give time to repair margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 33; calculation C3; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if EBITDA margin recovers toward 16.23% and total debt to EBITDA returns toward 2.88x while repurchases stay below free cash flow. It would worsen if last-twelve-month EBITDA falls further below USD 331.9 million, if the legal payment is funded by revolver borrowing, if a retailer reduces distribution, or if repurchases resume while the revolver is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1

fields.value: - Financial foundation ends at the balance sheet of 30 June 2026 and no fiscal 2026 results are supplied, so the leverage and liquidity conclusions describe that date, and the effect of the August legal payment on liquidity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No guidance or forecast is supplied, so the outlook rests on management discussion and recent trend and the downside path is qualitative.

fields.value: - Customer-level terms and shares by named retailer are not supplied, so the effect of losing one retailer cannot be sized and the downside path carries no stress figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen and margin has fallen while liquidity remains ample, as the table shows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths, in rank order. First, asset-light cash generation: additions to property were 0.20% of fiscal 2025 net sales and free cash flow was 67.79% of EBITDA over the last twelve months, so cash is available for debt service even as earnings fall, which supports debt service capacity. Second, liquidity and maturity runway: liquidity of USD 248.0 million and a first maturity 3.07 years away limit refinancing and liquidity risk in the near term. Third, brand scale: Premier Protein is 85.9% of sales and net sales grew 16.05% in fiscal 2025 and 2.28% in the nine months, which supports revenue durability while distribution holds. Fourth, no sponsor extraction and no dividend, so cash is not leaving through fees or distributions other than repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 53, 76; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses, in rank order. First, customer concentration: three retailers took 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales with no material long-term agreements, so one decision can remove a large share of revenue. Second, margin compression: EBITDA margin fell to 14.10% from 16.23% and cost of goods sold rose to 71.53% of net sales in the nine months, which cuts cash flow available for debt service. Third, rising leverage with shareholder returns above free cash flow: total debt to EBITDA rose to 3.42x from 2.88x while repurchases were 185.58% of free cash flow in fiscal 2025. Fourth, supply concentration and related-party reliance: one manufacturer made 46.3% of shake supply and shakes bought from a Post subsidiary reached 6.60% of nine-month cost of goods sold. Fifth, event risk from litigation, a USD 86.0 million legal payment and a leadership transition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 16–19; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BellRing sells ready-to-drink protein shakes and protein powders under Premier Protein and Dymatize, made by third-party contract manufacturers, which produce all shakes and most other products, and sold mainly through club, food, drug, mass and online retailers; it has one operating segment and about 530 employees, so the credit rests on brand pull and supply arrangements rather than on owned assets. The company was spun off from Post in March 2022 and Post sold its last shares in November 2022, so there is no sponsor or controlling holder identified, but the chairman holds a role at Post and Post's subsidiary supplies shakes, which links the borrower to its former parent through contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is likely to recur because the products are repeat-purchase staples, an analyst inference as no repeat-rate data is supplied, but it is concentrated and price-sensitive: three customers took 74.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales, the category is highly sensitive to pricing and promotion, and private label competes. Fiscal 2025 growth of 16.05% came from distribution gains and promotion; in the nine months Premier Protein volume rose 5% but its price fell, while Dymatize raised price, which shows pricing power in the smaller brand and not in the main one. The consequence for creditors is that revenue is durable only while the retailers keep the products listed, and that price support is weaker where most of the revenue sits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 31, 64; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C2; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Product costs are mostly per-unit tolling and ingredient charges but are held semi-fixed by minimum volume and take-or-pay commitments of USD 1,362.9 million, and inputs are protein, packaging and freight that are exposed to inflation and tariffs. Cost of goods sold rose to 71.53% of net sales in the nine months from 65.06%, and advertising rose to 4.21% of net sales from 3.54%, so the issuer is spending more to defend volume while input costs rise. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through pricing in powders and cost actions, but not against both input inflation and promotion at once; the evidence is that the second has already happened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 63, 66–67; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is very low, with additions to property at 0.20% of fiscal 2025 net sales and 0.47% in the nine months, and management states that no significant capital expenditure is planned for twelve months, so EBITDA converts to free cash flow at 67.79% before debt repayment. Working capital is the swing item: inventories absorbed USD 150.7 million of cash in the nine months against USD 128.3 million a year earlier. Cash taxes and interest are inside operating cash flow, and the legal payment will add a one-time outflow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Free cash flow is therefore available for debt service, but it has been directed to repurchases, not to deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 25; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense, with private label and competitors with greater resources; the main substitutes are private label and, as the issuer notes, weight-management medication that could reduce demand; buyer power is high because three customers take 74.0% of sales without long-term agreements; supplier power is meaningful because one manufacturer makes 46.3% of shake supply and a sole supplier provides the aseptic packaging; barriers to entry are not evidenced in the filings beyond brand and distribution, so the threat of new entrants is not established. Tariffs and trade policy are the policy factor that matters for credit, because they raise packaging and ingredient costs, and the other PEST factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are asset-light cash generation, brand scale, liquidity and a long maturity runway, and the absence of sponsor extraction; the weaknesses are customer concentration, compressed margin, rising leverage with shareholder returns above free cash flow, and supply concentration; the opportunities are Dymatize international growth and pricing and powder growth; the threats are tariffs, weight-management medication, private label and the securities litigation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, with USD 2,354.6 million of net sales over the last twelve months, low capital needs that keep free cash flow conversion at a steady level, liquidity of USD 248.0 million and a maturity runway of more than three years. The main constraints are diversification, which is weak by customer, product form and supplier, margin, which is weak at present, and financial policy, where repurchases above free cash flow have added debt. The trend is down on margin and leverage and steady on cash conversion. Ability to refinance cannot be tested because no rating or market data is supplied, and the missing data are the fiscal 2026 results, the covenant definitions and customer-level terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the headwinds are input-cost inflation including tariffs, promotional intensity on Premier Protein, the USD 86.0 million legal payment, litigation cost and a leadership transition; the tailwinds are distribution gains, Dymatize pricing and international volume, a pause in repurchases and a cost base with low capital needs. Management gives no guidance in the supplied filings, so the direction is inferred from trend: earnings pressure persists until price realisation or input costs turn. Over three to five years the issue is refinancing of USD 1,140.0 million of principal in fiscal 2030, which will be priced on the leverage and margin the company shows by then; the category is described by management as rapidly growing, which is management language, not evidence of credit strength.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 63; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 20–22, 33; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is one of the three large retailers reducing shelf space or moving volume to a competing or private-label shake, which the company cannot contract against because it has no material long-term supply agreements with customers. The first operational break is volume falling below the minimum quantities committed to contract manufacturers and suppliers, which can bring penalties or payments for product not taken; the financial transmission is lower gross profit on a margin that is already compressed, a larger inventory build, and operating cash flow that falls faster than sales. The consequence is higher leverage than the 3.42x total debt to EBITDA reported at 30 June 2026, drawing on the USD 500.0 million revolver (USD 197.6 million undrawn after letters of credit) to fund the USD 86.0 million legal payment and any resumed repurchases, and a weaker position ahead of the refinancing in fiscal 2030. Management levers are the repurchase programme, advertising and inventory; resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall in the near term but not to keep leverage from rising, and the observable triggers are in the monitoring table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_brbr_brbr-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14, 31, 66–67, 93–95; 10-Q_2026-06-30_brbr_brbr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–13, 16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, BellRing presents an adequate business profile supported by asset-light cash generation, brand scale and a long maturity runway, but credit quality is constrained by customer and supplier concentration, compressed margin and rising leverage. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow conversion has held at 67.79% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage and margin in fiscal 2030, with no rating or market data to test it. The primary downside path is a retailer cutting distribution against fixed purchase commitments. Further analysis would require the fiscal 2026 results, the executed credit documents and customer-level terms. Top risk: customer concentration combined with compressed margin.
